headline: NTSB: Steering Casualty Before Riverboat Hit
subheadline: What the tanker's VDR shows so far
insight: NTSB: VDR data shows Atlantic Asphalt's rudder stayed to starboard about two minutes before it struck the moored American Heritage. Root cause not yet determined.

sources.title: NTSB says tanker suffered 'steering casualty' before New Orleans riverboat crash

factCheck.notes: UPDATE to HM-2026-111401 (cards 14 Nov and 15 Nov 08:22). NTSB on-site briefing Sun 15 Nov (Board Member John DeLeeuw, senior investigator Bart Barnum), corroborated by Fox News, ABC News, Reuters via gCaptain, MarEx and Splash247: preliminary VDR data shows a 'steering casualty resulting in the rudder remaining to starboard'; tanker veered toward the east bank; steering problem began about 12:26, impact about 12:28 local (Fox; Splash247 'two minutes before impact'); VDR (9+ hours) captured whistle, radio requests for assistance, anchor and emergency shiphandling orders; riverboat capsized about 22 minutes after impact; ~140 passengers and 50 crew aboard American Heritage, 19 crew aboard the tanker; preliminary report expected in about 30 days; tanker crew interviews from 16 Nov. NTSB stressed 'steering casualty' does not establish the cause, so headlines saying 'steering failure caused' are not followed.

meta.description: At an on-site briefing on 15 November 2026 the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board said preliminary voyage data recorder data shows the asphalt tanker Atlantic Asphalt suffered a steering casualty that left its rudder to starboard about two minutes before it struck American Cruise Lines' moored riverboat American Heritage at New Orleans on 13 November. The tanker veered toward the east bank; the recorder captured the ship's whistle, radio calls for assistance, orders to let go the anchors and emergency shiphandling orders, and the riverboat capsized about 22 minutes after impact with everyone aboard accounted for. NTSB said the term does not establish the root cause, which is still under investigation; tanker crew interviews start this week and a preliminary report is expected in about 30 days.
